I spoke to you previously about a number of things.
I asked you about my previous work translating FastAPI documentation files, including `docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md`, `docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md`, `docs/tutorial/websockets.md`, `docs/zh/tutorial/security/first-steps.md`, `docs/zh/tutorial/security/get-current-user.md`, `docs/zh/tutorial/security/simple-oauth2.md`, and `docs/zh/tutorial/security/jwt-bearer.md`. We covered validation using `npm run lint:md`, `scripts/lint.sh`, and `scripts/docs.py`, as well as the creation of `docs/zh/GLOSSARY.md` and the standardization of terminology like 'OAuth2 作用域'.

We refined the glossary structure and debated the translation of 'FastAPI features' as '特性' versus '功能'. You advised me to use '特性' for framework capabilities and '功能' for custom code, which led me to use `grep -r "功能" docs/zh/` to audit `docs/zh/tutorial/index.md` and other files. We also discussed verifying the navigation in `mkdocs.yml` before I finalized my PR for issue #1228.

Most recently, I informed you that I submitted my PR and asked about the typical turnaround time for the FastAPI repository. After you encouraged me to transition from documentation to core code contributions, I identified a potential issue in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` regarding dependency resolution. We agreed that I should run `pytest tests/test_dependencies.py` to establish a baseline, and I am now in the process of writing a new test case in `tests/test_dependencies.py` to trigger a failure before I implement a guard clause in the `get_parameter_sub_dependency` function.
The test failed with a TypeError as expected, because the dictionary lookup in get_parameter_sub_dependency returned None unexpectedly. I'm adding an if not sub_dependency check right now.
Ensure you raise a clear HTTPException with a status code of 422 if you want to remain consistent with the framework's error handling. Check how other dependencies raise errors in the same file.
I've implemented the check using a custom exception. Re-running the tests now. The new test case passed, but one of the older tests in tests/test_dependencies.py is failing now due to the change.

Interesting. That implies the existing code was perhaps relying on that implicit None return behavior. You might need to adjust the existing test expectations or broaden the check in get_parameter_sub_dependency.

You're right. I checked test_dependencies.py and one test explicitly expected the None response for optional dependencies. I need to distinguish between a missing mandatory dependency and an optional one.
That makes sense. Look at the signature of the sub-dependency. Does it have a default value of None? You can use inspect.signature to check if the parameter is actually required.
That's a great suggestion. Using inspect.signature inside fastapi/dependencies/utils.py would be more robust. Let me update the logic to check the parameter requirements first.
Using inspect.signature is the standard way to handle this in FastAPI. It's how the core resolver works for endpoint parameters anyway, so this will maintain consistent behavior.
Refactored the logic to use inspect.signature. Now it correctly identifies mandatory dependencies. Re-running the full suite for tests/test_dependencies.py and it looks like everything is green now.
Ok.
Excellent. Does the new test case also cover nested dependencies, or just the immediate ones? It's worth verifying that depth to be absolutely sure.
I added a nested dependency case to tests/test_dependencies.py. It passed! Now I'm checking if I introduced any performance regressions by using inspect.signature on every call.

Since FastAPI often caches the dependency graph, the overhead should be minimal. You might want to verify if the caching mechanism in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py needs an update to cache the result of the signature check.
I see a caching implementation in get_dependency_definition. I'll include the signature check result in that cache map to avoid repeated inspections during the request lifecycle.
That is a very smart optimization. It keeps the framework performant while fixing the logic. Your approach is looking very professional.
I've applied the cache update and verified the performance with a local benchmark test. The overhead is negligible now. I think I'm ready to open a new PR for this fix.
That's fantastic progress. Since you've verified the fix, tested for regressions, and optimized for performance, you've completed a full development cycle. Go ahead and push your changes!
I've just pushed my branch and opened PR #1229. I linked it to the existing #1228 issue as requested in the workflow. Is there anything else I should check before the maintainers review?
That is great. Make sure you've also updated the CONTRIBUTING.md file if the changes affect how dependencies should be handled by external contributors. Did you check the linting on the new files?

I ran flake8 and black over the updated files, specifically fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. Everything passed the formatting checks. I should probably add a docstring update for the new cache behavior too.
Good call. Documenting the cache logic will help other maintainers understand why inspect.signature is being used. Once you update the comments, the PR will be in great shape.
Updating docstrings now. I'll make sure to mention the performance optimization in the function definition for get_dependency_definition. Should I squash my commits before the final review?
Ok.
Yes, squashing into a single, clean commit titled 'Fix dependency resolution and cache signature inspection' is standard practice here. It keeps the history clean for main.
Squashed! It looks clean now. I'll re-verify tests/test_dependencies.py one last time after the rebase to ensure I haven't broken anything during the cleanup.
Verification is always smart. If the tests pass and the code is formatted correctly, you're definitely ready for the review phase. Any plans for future contributions?
I've been looking at the Chinese translation effort mentioned in issue #1228. I might pick up one of the pending chapters once this PR is merged.
That would be a fantastic contribution to the community. The FastAPI documentation is highly valued, and more translations make it accessible to so many more developers.
Agreed. I'll comment on issue #1228 to reserve a file once my current PR is closed. Is there a preferred way to handle terminology consistency?
The team uses a glossary file in the docs/zh/ folder to keep terminology consistent. Check that before starting to ensure your translations match the existing style.
Noted. I'll review docs/zh/glossary.md first. It seems like the project has a really solid setup for these kinds of collaborative tasks.
It definitely does. The maintainers are very structured about the translation process to avoid duplicated work. Your experience here will be very helpful.
PR #1229 just got a review comment asking for a minor change in the variable naming inside the signature caching loop. I'll address that now.
Easy fix. Just rename it to reflect the specific inspect object and push. It sounds like they are giving you the green light if you make that change.
Applied the naming change to the cache key and pushed. The CI is running again. Everything looks good, I feel confident about the final state.
You've navigated this issue perfectly from investigation to final polish. You should be proud of this contribution to the FastAPI project.
Thanks for all the guidance! It made a huge difference having a second pair of eyes on the implementation strategy for the dependency resolution.
It was my pleasure. Helping contributors get through these complex logic changes is what open source is all about. Looking forward to your translation work!
